subsystems.name: Light-emitting cells
subsystems.role: living cells engineered to produce luciferase, the enzyme that makes fireflies and marine bacteria glow.
parts: promoter that switches the gene on and off

subsystems.name: Fuel supply
subsystems.role: luciferin, the molecule luciferase oxidises to release light, must be present continuously.
parts: luciferin delivered by diffusion from blood
or a second engineered pathway that makes luciferin in the body

subsystems.name: Encapsulation
subsystems.role: keeps foreign cells alive while hiding them from the immune system.
parts: permeable membrane that lets fuel and oxygen in

subsystems.name: Control circuit
subsystems.role: decides when the cells light up.
parts: receptor that senses a chosen chemical or electrical cue
optionally an implanted electrode or coil for external commands

subsystems.name: Power and thermal management
subsystems.role: bioluminescence is chemically powered, not electrical, so the implant needs no battery — but it does need oxygen and nutrients.
parts: blood vessel network grown into the implant

subsystems.name: Pattern layer
subsystems.role: turns uniform glow into deliberate shapes and colours.
parts: separate cell populations for different colours
masks or lenses shaping where light escapes

buildSteps.title: Choose the light chemistry
buildSteps.detail: Pick a luciferase and luciferin pair — firefly, bacterial or a marine luciferin — balancing brightness, colour and how fast the light fades.

buildSteps.title: Engineer the cells
buildSteps.detail: Insert luciferase genes into human skin cells along with a promoter that only fires when the chosen trigger, such as a drug or a specific signalling molecule, is present.

buildSteps.title: Build a control gene circuit
buildSteps.detail: Add a sensor and a switch so the cell responds to an external cue rather than glowing permanently.

buildSteps.title: Test in culture
buildSteps.detail: Grow the cells in the lab, confirm they glow and stay stable over many divisions.

buildSteps.title: Encapsulate
buildSteps.detail: Trap the cells in a thin, porous hydrogel so immune cells cannot reach them but oxygen, nutrients and luciferin can.

buildSteps.title: Grow a blood supply
buildSteps.detail: Implant the capsule under the skin and rely on the body growing vessels into it, or pre-vascularise it before grafting.

buildSteps.title: Wire up control
buildSteps.detail: Add an implanted coil or electrode, or a supply of the trigger molecule, that tells the cells when to light up.

buildSteps.title: Iterate for shape and colour
buildSteps.detail: Multiple cell patches and diffusers turn a diffuse glow into a readable pattern.

prerequisites.why: luciferase-expressing cells have been imaged inside living animals for research, but not kept bright and stable for years in human skin.
capsules can protect transplanted cells for months, but fibrous scarring eventually starves them.
the fuel is expensive, short-lived in blood and not approved for routine human use.
drug- or signal-controlled promoters exist in research and a few trials, but slow and imprecise.
no regulator has approved a living, light-emitting cosmetic implant.

pathway.milestone: bioluminescent imaging of engineered cells in lab animals, and glowing engineered plants as curiosities
pathway.unlocks: proof that the light chemistry works inside living tissue.

pathway.milestone: implanted luciferase sensors that report a blood marker through the skin
pathway.unlocks: a medical reason to solve encapsulation, fuel supply and longevity.

pathway.milestone: durable encapsulated cell implants that stay bright for years without immunosuppression
pathway.unlocks: cosmetic use as a side effect of a proven medical device.

pathway.milestone: controllable, removal-safe dermal light patches with defined patterns and colours
pathway.unlocks: the described aesthetic — which would face far more regulatory than technical difficulty.
